PHASE VI: THE IMPERIAL ROOT (The Ethiopian Sovereignty)

1. The Kebra Nagast (The Glory of Kings) The fundamental blueprint of the Solomonic dynasty. This is your study of the Divine Mandate and the origin of the national signal.
2. The Fetha Nagast (The Law of the Kings) The traditional legal code. This is where you study how justice was structured before modern systems—the "Baseline" of Ethiopian order.
3. The Life and Progress of Emperor Haile Selassie I His autobiography. You are studying the Diplomatic Architecture of a man who spoke to the world and forced it to listen.
4. The Chronicles of Emperor Menelik II Study the Battle of Adwa not as a war, but as a Masterclass in Systemic Unity. He synchronized different tribes and frequencies to defeat a colonial machine.
5. Empress Taytu Betul: Lioness of Ethiopia She is the "Parisian Modern" equivalent of her time—sophisticated, strategic, and uncompromising. She is essential for understanding the Balance of Power.
6. The Ethiopian Tewahedo Church Architecture & Art
To inform your Parisian + Aesthetic goal. The geometry of Lalibela and the colors of Gondar are the original "Sacred Practices."
7. Works by Afewerk Tekle
Study his visual language. He combined modern techniques with Ethiopian soul—exactly what you are doing with the "Hasselblad" look.
8. The Oromo Gadaa System: An Indigenous African Democracy
Study the Systemic Thinking of the Gadaa. It is one of the most sophisticated social structures in history—perfect for your "Free Spirit" logic.
9. Tsegaye Gabre-Medhin’s Poetry and Plays
To help with your creative writing and lyricism. He understood the "Highs and Lows" of the Ethiopian spirit.
10. Pillars of Ethiopian History by Taddesse Tamrat

THE SYSTEMIC ARCHIVES
